outcomeNote: Rejected on a semantic mismatch: the assumed invariant did not hold.
changedBeliefs: Skipping per-cell `sqlite3_column_type()` by caching first-row storage classes is not safe as a hidden `selectBytes()` default. SQLite storage class is per value, not per column: a local probe with an untyped column containing row 1 INTEGER and row 2 TEXT produced `[{"v":1},{"v":0}]` from the prototype while `select()` saw `[{"v":1},{"v":"abc"}]`.

There is plausible fixed-shape headroom in wide rows: `select_bytes_wide_cols.dart` measured candidate-faster on 10k-row integer and mixed-column shapes in both pass orderings. The magnitude is not load-bearing because the flipped baseline drifted much slower than the first baseline, but one `sqlite3_column_type()` call per cell is not free.

The integer-heavy focused harness did not reproduce a clean win: only 10k x 8 small ints improved (-7.7%), while 10k x 20 small ints (+10.3%), 10k x 20 big ints (+3.9%), the mixed guard (+4.0%), and 1k x 2 ints (+6.6%) regressed in the same pass. A per-query type vector plus altered branch shape can erase the saved type probe on the rows that should have been the cleanest path.
nextSignals: Do not skip `sqlite3_column_type()` in the general `selectBytes()` path based only on first-row type stability.

Reopen stable-type JSON encoding only with a real proof surface: SQLite STRICT tables, declared-type plus query-shape constraints, generated/static statement metadata, or an explicit user-visible mode that documents dynamic-type behavior.

If such a proof surface appears, use `select_bytes_wide_cols.dart` as the fast ceiling check and add a dynamic-storage-class correctness guard before accepting any production runtime code. The rejected prototype is preserved at `archive/exp-200`.
